correctness.rationale: Disjointly count palindromes containing zero, one, two, or three 1s. The per-gap classes yield the exact formula for all n≥3; a minimal-largest-gap integer argument and comparison with repeated-gap values prove the sharp n≥14 maxima and complete optimizer list. Standalone independent string enumeration checked 2300 ordered triples through n=25; independent analytic enumeration checked 2,274,994 triples through n=240. Finite checks corroborate, not replace, the arbitrary-n proof.

evidence: Simpson 2014 abstract: every circular length-n word has fewer than \(5n/3\) palindromic factors, and an n divisible by three construction attains \(5n/3-2\).
The present restricted maxima are 5m-2, 5m-1, and 5m+1 in the three residues; the generic \(5n/3\) upper bound has nonzero slack and no restricted extremizer classification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The known general inequality is stronger in domain but weaker in precision; it does not imply equality for all three-one words or characterize maximizers. The accessible earlier fixed-weight-three results concern linear palindromic defect and unbordered cyclic shifts rather than the distinct circular palindrome spectrum.
The new gap classification distinguishes the all-distinct, exactly-two-equal, and all-equal regimes and identifies all maximizing dihedral classes for every n at least fourteen.

Linear palindromic defect and circular unbordered-shift counts are different invariants and do not algebraically determine the length-bounded set of distinct circular palindromes.

originality.rationale: Simpson 2014 already supplies a general \(5n/3\) bound and near-sharp Biggles construction, explicitly acknowledged. The current statement classifies counts for every triple, all restricted maximizing triples in every residue class, and exact distance from restricted optimality. Completed database, literature, and accessible prior-claim comparisons found no identical or dominating characterization. Unavailable full text of the closest article leaves a specified residual risk, not an unqualified novelty certificate.
residual_risks: The uninspected full body of Simpson (2014), especially Lemma 6, could contain implicit or explicit stronger specialized enumeration; public metadata alone cannot exclude this.
Unindexed studies of circular palindrome counts restricted by fixed Hamming weight might include an equivalent formula.

value.rationale: This is a natural sparsity boundary of the classic circular-palindrome extremal problem. Unlike re-evaluating the known Biggles witness, it gives an all-length complete gap-spectral classification and sharp optimizer uniqueness/orbit counts; the distinct-gap law quantifies how the largest gap controls lost palindromes and explains the near-\(5n/3\) extremal phenomenon. The claim is confined to fixed weight three and does not assert unrestricted maxima.
